extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants (PIs, postdocs, early-stage investigators) seeking funding/process guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Practical Q&A guidance for applicants navigating NIH funding decisions, eRA Commons statuses, interactions with Program Officers (POs), institutional/grants-management steps (JIT, transfers, pre-award), and resubmission strategy for mechanisms like R01, K99/R00, K23, F32, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact Program Officer about resubmission and FOA renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact your PO early with two questions: should you resubmit on the upcoming due date, and will the PAR/FOA be renewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POs can advise whether to resubmit and can give resubmission strategy (what reviewers focused on). PO optimism does not guarantee funding. If PO recommends resubmission, ask about FOA renewal so you know if additional submission opportunities exist. Ask after you receive the summary statement (POs need the summary to comment on funding likelihood).

rubrics_metrics.name: IC Directors make final funding decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: IC Directors make all final funding decisions; councils only approve a long list for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council approval produces a paylist for the IC Director to consider; not every application on that list will receive an award. The IC Director, not the Council, signs the Notice of Award (NOA) and makes final selections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council approves long list but does not guarantee awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Council approves a long list of applications for the IC Director to consider for funding; approval does not equal an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More applications are placed on the paylist than can be funded to provide back-up in case higher-ranked applications drop out or money is reallocated. Being on the list means consideration but is not a guarantee.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons status interpretation (Pending / Award Prepared / Council Review Completed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Status changes such as 'Council review completed', 'Pending', and 'Award prepared' have specific operational meanings and do not guarantee funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Award prepared' usually means the award is waiting for IC Director signoff (could be hours to a week+). 'Pending' can indicate administrative review or other bookkeeping and can last months. A change back to 'Council review completed' can just be bookkeeping. Only direct JIT requests and explicit status changes indicating administrative processing give stronger signals—but none are guarantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: If you move institutions after submission, notify PO and arrange transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Your institution should be willing to transfer the application, but NIH must approve the new institution as capable of conducting the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify the PO as soon as possible (ideally before a move). The prior institution may want to keep budgeted portions; NIH does not adjudicate institutional negotiations but must approve facilities/resources/personnel at the new institution. Alternatively, if the application has not been reviewed, you could withdraw and resubmit from your new institution (requires the old institution to withdraw it too).

rubrics_metrics.name: Start date can be negotiated but may be constrained by FY and IC policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed start dates are guidelines; ICs may be unwilling to commit to later start dates during FY-end processing and may revisit Other Support prior to issuing a delayed NOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want to delay start (e.g., from April to mid-August), ask the PO well in advance and have an acceptable rationale. IC policies vary; some may need to re-review Other Support if start is delayed. The award must be issued within the fiscal year (Sept 30) if it is to count for that FY's funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret impact scores with percentiles and IC-specific paylines
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact scores alone are less informative without percentiles and knowledge of the IC's payline; ICs vary and sometimes use different payline practices for ESIs/new investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An impact score (e.g., 23) may be competitive depending on percentile and IC payline. Check IC interim/final paylines; some ICs have separate paylines or priority for ESIs/new investigators (e.g., inclusion up to Xth percentile). Paylines can change across FYs and may be affected by budget changes and number of applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare Just-in-Time (JIT) materials when requested or proactively check with GMS
rubrics_metrics.description: If JIT has not been requested, wait for a request; if you haven’t submitted JIT and think it would help, ask the Grants Management Specialist (GMS) or PO whether to prepare/submit it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have already submitted JIT, it will be under review during administrative processing. GMS can advise on timing and whether you should proactively submit JIT; preparing JIT materials (e.g., Other Support) in advance is often prudent.

rubrics_metrics.name: DRR assignment requires IC acceptance; ICs can refuse or skip applications
rubrics_metrics.description: CSR/DRR only assigns applications after an IC accepts them; an IC can refuse applications if they don't fit the mission, and applications with fundable scores can still be skipped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IC refusal often occurs when the science fits another IC or the IC is not participating in the FOA. Applications may be skipped (within payline but not picked) when an IC seeks to balance portfolio gaps or is oversubscribed in particular areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications may be 'skipped' or subject to portfolio priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Even applications within the payline can be skipped if the IC is oversubscribed in a specific scientific area or has portfolio-balancing needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is more likely for research awards than K awards, though it can happen; POs may advocate for select pay, and you should discuss with PO if you are on the bubble.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNAP indicator meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: SNAP indicates eligibility for Streamlined Noncompeting Award Procedures (SNAP), not that an application is about to be funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SNAP eligibility is an administrative indicator; not every SNAP-eligible application on a paylist receives an award. Direct JIT requests and status changes to 'Pending' or 'Pending administrative review' are stronger operational signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award spending allowance (up to 90 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions may begin pre-award spending up to 90 days before the award start date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-award spending requires the institution to set up appropriate accounts; it can be used to cover salary until the NOA is issued, but institutions vary in how they manage this. Verify with your sponsored programs office/grants office.

rubrics_metrics.name: GMS handles award processing; PO is separate from award issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants Management Specialists and institutional AORs handle award processing and paperwork; Program Officers do not control the operational issuance of awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POs can advise and advocate but are typically not involved in the GMS workflow that actually prepares the NOA. For timing/status questions about award setup, contact GMS or institutional grants administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate concurrent/overlapping awards carefully (e.g., F32 to K99 transitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If terminating one award and beginning another (e.g., F32 terminating early for K99 start), coordinate termination and start dates carefully to avoid funding gaps and administrative delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should not terminate existing support until there is assurance of overlap or pre-award coverage. Mistakes/delays in institutional paperwork can cause gaps; check other support accuracy (errors can delay NOA). Discuss transitions early with institutional offices and PO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Support is reviewed and can affect delayed starts or award issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs may review Other Support before issuing an award if a start date is delayed or to confirm no conflicting commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you request a delayed start, ICs may want updated Other Support documentation; ensure Other Support is accurate and current to avoid processing delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: applications submitted in one calendar year are often for next fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications submitted in one calendar year are often considered for the following fiscal year; payline and budget decisions align with FY cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can affect whether your application falls within a particular FY's payline and how budget cuts/increases in an IC affect funding likelihood. Be mindful of FY timing when planning resubmissions or start-date negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PO advocacy is helpful but cannot promise funding
rubrics_metrics.description: POs can advocate for applications and advise on strategy but generally avoid making guarantees about funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POs may suggest whether to resubmit, recommend preparing JIT, or provide insight from the review meeting, but they will often speak cautiously to avoid creating expectations. If in doubt, ask if the PO would recommend an A0 in a certain timeframe so you can plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to contact PO: after summary statement
rubrics_metrics.description: POs typically need to see the summary statement before commenting on funding likelihood or giving detailed advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although informal early contact is fine for procedural questions, concrete advice about resubmission or funding likelihood generally requires the summary statement (POs do not see summary statements sooner than applicants).
